confirmation.label: Small heading of a card in the chat that shows a request waiting for someone's yes.
confirmation.confirm: Label of the button on a request card that gives the yes.
confirmation.refuse: Label of the button on a request card that says no.
confirmation.proof.title: Heading of the block on a request card where the person proves who they are.
confirmation.proof.passkey: Label of the button that starts the proof with a passkey.
confirmation.proof.password: Label of the field where the person types their password to prove who they are.
confirmation.proof.submit: Label of the button that sends the proof.
confirmation.changed: Line under a request card that tells the request was changed before it was carried out.
confirmation.nudged: Line under a request card that tells the one who asked reminded the person.
chat.key.frame_title: Accessible title of the frame that holds the secure form where the key is typed.
chat.key.action.rekey: Label of the button on a card that opens the form to type the key again.
chat.key.action.add: Label of the button on a card that opens the form to add a key.
chat.key.action.check: Label of the button on a card that checks that the server of the model answers.
chat.key.action.admin: Label of the button on a card that opens the form to type the admin key.
chat.key.waiting: Shown in the chat while the person has not yet typed the key in the form.
chat.key.checked: Shown in the chat once the new key was tested and the model answered.
account.title: Main title of the page where a person manages their own account.
account.display_name: Label of the line that shows the name of the person on their account page.
account.username: Label of the line that shows the sign-in name on the account page.
account.role: Label of the line that shows the role of the person in the household on the account page.
account.name.label: Label of the field where the person types their new name.
account.name.submit: Label of the button that saves the new name.
account.password.current: Label of the field where the person types the password they use now.
account.password.new: Label of the field where the person types the new password.
account.password.confirm: Label of the field where the person types the new password a second time.
account.password.submit: Label of the button that saves the new password.
account.passkeys.heading: Heading of the section of the account page about passkeys.
account.passkeys.remove: Label of the button that removes one passkey from the list.
account.passkeys.label: Label of the field where the person names the passkey they add.
account.passkeys.current: Label of the field where the person types their password before adding a passkey.
account.passkeys.submit: Label of the button that starts adding a passkey.
vault.form.title: Title of the secure page where a person types the secret the assistant asked for, which goes straight into the vault: the key of a model provider, a token, or the user name and password of one account. It asks for that one secret and nothing else: no other password, no code, no other information.
vault.form.purpose: Label of the line that tells what the secret is for (the line itself is written elsewhere: the key of a model provider, or the name of an account and where it is put in a request).
vault.form.destinations: Label of the list of the only addresses the secret will ever be sent to: the vault shows each address after it, as a host name, without words.
vault.form.value_label: Label of the one field of the secure page, where the person types the key or the token the assistant asked for (an account of a user name and a password has two fields instead). It asks for that one secret and nothing else: no other password, no code, no other information.
vault.form.user_label: Label of the field of the secure page where the person types the user name of the account the assistant asked for, when that account is a user name and a password.
vault.form.password_label: Label of the field of the secure page where the person types the password of that same account, under its user name. It asks for the password of that one account and nothing else.
vault.form.submit: Label of the button that saves the secret in the vault.
vault.form.privacy: Shown on the secure page where the person types a secret (a key, a token, or the user name and password of one account): what becomes of it. It asks for that one secret and nothing else: no other password, no code, no other information.
vault.form.error.length: Shown on the secure page when what was typed in a field is empty or too long: {max} is the most characters it may have. It asks for that one secret and nothing else: no other password, no code, no other information.
vault.form.error.invalid: Shown on the secure page when what was typed holds characters that cannot be kept. It asks for that one secret and nothing else: no other password, no code, no other information.
action.card.done.note.show: The card under the assistant's reply that shows the person the exact words someone wrote when they left a note for them, exactly as they were typed. {name} is who wrote them; {when} is the date and time they were written; {words} is filled by the code with those words, which may run over several lines: keep it as it is, after the rest of the sentence.
action.card.done.note.show.noted: The card under the assistant's reply that shows the person a note someone left for them when their exact words were not kept: it must say plainly that these are not the author's own words but what the assistant noted. {name} is who left the note; {when} is when; {words} is filled by the code with what the assistant noted, which may run over several lines: keep it as it is, after the rest of the sentence.
action.card.done.note.show.his: The card under the assistant's reply that shows the person a note the assistant left them himself, in his own name: the words are his own. {when} is when he wrote it; {words} is filled by the code with his words, which may run over several lines: keep it as it is, after the rest of the sentence.
action.card.phrase_agree_opened: The card under the assistant's reply that tells the person he is now listening for the phrase they want to agree as a spoken proof, then for them to say it again. It must never contain, ask for or hint at the phrase itself.
action.card.phrase_removed_theirs: The card under the assistant's reply that tells the person who asked that someone else's spoken phrase was removed (the owner's, or an adult's for a child): the assistant no longer knows it, and that person is left a word about it.
action.card.phrase_removed_theirs_untold: The card under the assistant's reply that tells the person who asked that someone else's spoken phrase is no longer known to the assistant, when no word could be left to that person (they had no phrase, or are no longer in the household): it must not say they will be told.
action.card.refused.not_weighed: The card under the assistant's reply when something only his judgement may let go (someone else's spoken phrase removed) could not be weighed now: nothing was done, nothing is asked of the person, and they may ask again a little later.
action.card.phrase_removed: The card under the assistant's reply that tells the person their spoken phrase was removed: the assistant no longer knows it and it can no longer be used as a proof.
action.card.voice_unlearnt: The card under the assistant's reply that tells the person he forgot what he had learnt of their voice, so that it can be learnt again.
chat.key.new.kind: Label of the list where the person chooses the provider of a new key of their own.
chat.key.new.base_url_hint: Help under the field of a server's address: {local} and {remote} are two example addresses.
chat.key.new.has_key: Label of the box the person ticks when their own server needs an API key.
chat.key.new.submit: Label of the button that sends the choice of the provider of a new key.
chat.key.new.checking: Shown under the form of a new key while the assistant checks that the model answers.
chat.key.new.name.title: Heading of the question asked when the server of a new key does not list its models.
chat.key.new.name.submit: Label of the button that sends the name of the model the server serves.
chat.key.secret_purpose: What the secure form of the vault says the key typed in it is for.
audit.who.system: Who did it, in a line of the audit log, when it was the assistant himself and not a person: a name, not a sentence.
audit.line.other: A line of the audit log for something done that has no line of its own yet.
audit.outcome.executed: The end of a line of the audit log, after a colon: what came of a person's answer to a request. A few words, not a sentence.
audit.outcome.failed: The end of a line of the audit log, after a colon: what came of a person's answer to a request. A few words, not a sentence.

audit.outcome.not_yours: The end of a line of the audit log, after a colon: what came of a person's answer to a request. A few words, not a sentence.
audit.outcome.needs_explicit: The end of a line of the audit log, after a colon: what came of a person's answer to a request. A few words, not a sentence.
audit.outcome.needs_proof: The end of a line of the audit log, after a colon: what came of a person's answer to a request. A few words, not a sentence.
audit.outcome.proof_failed: The end of a line of the audit log, after a colon: what came of a person's answer to a request. A few words, not a sentence.

audit.outcome.arrived: The end of a line of the audit log, after a colon: what came of a person's answer to a request. A few words, not a sentence.
audit.outcome.asked_again: The end of a line of the audit log, after a colon: what came of a person's answer to a request. A few words, not a sentence.
audit.outcome.writer_asks: The end of a line of the audit log, after a colon: what came of a person's answer to a request. A few words, not a sentence.
audit.verdict.do: The end of a line of the audit log, after a colon: what the assistant decided to do about an action asked of him. A few words, not a sentence.
audit.verdict.yes: The end of a line of the audit log, after a colon: what the assistant decided to do about an action asked of him. A few words, not a sentence.

audit.verdict.do_not: The end of a line of the audit log, after a colon: what the assistant decided to do about an action asked of him. A few words, not a sentence.
audit.barrier.allow: The end of a line of the audit log, after a colon: what the rules of the household decided about an action. A few words, not a sentence.
audit.barrier.needs_approval: The end of a line of the audit log, after a colon: what the rules of the household decided about an action. A few words, not a sentence.
audit.barrier.refuse: The end of a line of the audit log, after a colon: what the rules of the household decided about an action. A few words, not a sentence.
manifest.description: One-line description of the assistant that a phone shows when the page is installed as an app.
action.describe.texts.language: {language} is a language tag, such as es, fr or pt-BR.
action.describe.texts.for_someone.langua: {language} is a language tag, such as es, fr or pt-BR.
action.describe.texts.language_version: {language} is a language tag, such as es, fr or pt-BR.
action.describe.texts.language.house: {language} is a language tag, such as es, fr or pt-BR.
chat.author.assistant: Accessible label of a bubble of the assistant in the chat; {domo} is the name the reader calls the assistant by (the assistant unless they gave him another).
chat.input.placeholder: Placeholder of the message box of the chat; {domo} is the name the reader calls the assistant by (the assistant unless they gave him another).
chat.status.writing: Line for screen readers while a reply is being written; {domo} is the name the reader calls the assistant by.
chat.actions.label: Accessible label of the cards of what the assistant did under a reply; {domo} is the name the reader calls the assistant by.
voice.turn_on: Label of the button, on the chat page, that turns the voice on: from then on the page listens through the microphone.
voice.turn_off: Label of the button, on the chat page, that turns the voice off: the page stops listening at once.
voice.listening: Line next to the voice button, shown only while the microphone is open and the voice can hear: the page is listening right now.
voice.talk: Label of the button, on the chat page, held down to speak to the assistant when the house hears only what is said with a gesture (the owner chose so, as no model at home can tell whether a sentence is said to the assistant); shown only then.
voice.on_gesture: Line next to the voice button while the house hears only what is said with the button held: the microphone is open, but nothing is sent unless the person holds the button.
voice.off: Line next to the voice button while the voice is off: the page does not listen.
voice.preparing: Line next to the voice button while the page opens the microphone and loads what it needs to tell speech from noise; the page does not listen yet.
voice.unavailable: Line next to the voice button when the connection to the house for the voice is down or the house cannot hear yet; the page keeps trying and nothing said is kept meanwhile.
voice.no_microphone: Line next to the voice button when no microphone is connected to this device, so the voice cannot be turned on.
voice.refused_by_browser: Line next to the voice button when the browser refused the microphone to this page (the person said no, or a setting blocks it); the person can allow it in the browser's settings for this site.
voice.moved: Line next to the voice button when another tab or device of the same household took over the voice: this page no longer listens, and the button takes the voice back.
voice.reload: Line next to the voice button when this tab was opened for someone else and must be reloaded before the voice can be used.
voice.not_taken_elsewhere: Notice under the voice button when the house took a sentence of this page's microphone as heard by another page of the same person: nothing was done with it here; the person can say it again.
voice.not_taken_now: Notice under the voice button when the sentence just heard was not taken: said by a voice the house does not know that was not answered, or while the microphone was kept for another person's words (their secret phrase being agreed). It must not say which, nor that a voice was not recognised or that a phrase is awaited: someone imitating a voice must learn nothing from it.
voice.failed: Notice under the voice button when what was said could not be answered because of a failure of the house; the person can say it again or write it.
voice.not_told: Notice under the voice button when what was said could not be given to the assistant (he was busy answering, say); the person can say it again.
voice.speaking: Line under the voice button while the assistant's voice is coming out of the speakers (replaces 'Listening' for that time); it says what is true, nothing more.
voice.cannot_speak: Notice under the voice button when the assistant's voice could not speak a reply (a failure of the speech service); the reply stays written in the discussion and the rest of it is not said.
voice.cannot_speak_preparing: Notice under the voice button when the speech service is still getting its models ready, so the reply is not said aloud; it stays written in the discussion; it will work later.
voice.cannot_speak_limit: Notice under the voice button when a firm spending limit stopped the voice; the reply stays written in the discussion; the owner can change the limit.
voice.cannot_speak_no_model: Notice under the voice button when no model is chosen for speaking (or the one chosen is not offered); the reply stays written in the discussion.
voice.cannot_play: Notice under the voice button when this browser could not play the sound (the sound is blocked until the person touches the page, or the browser cannot play it); the reply stays written in the discussion.
voice.phrase_removed_word: A word the assistant leaves, as his own, to someone whose spoken phrase (a proof said aloud) was removed at the request of someone with a say over it (the owner, or an adult for a child); he tells it in his own words at their next visit. Says that it was removed on someone else's request and that a new one can be agreed; never the phrase, never who asked unless he judges it right to say.
voice.prints_erased_word: A word the assistant leaves, as his own, to someone whose learnt voice he erased on his own (he judged it wrong or useless); he tells it in his own words at their next visit. Says only that it was erased and will be learnt again, never why nor who else spoke.
talk.no_key: Said by the text program (a terminal) when the person's message was refused because the assistant has no model key yet.
talk.too_long: Said by the text program when the message typed was refused for being longer than the allowed length.
talk.not_sayable: Said by the text program when the server cannot take the message typed (for example it is empty or not text).
talk.held_back: Said by the text program when the server refuses for too many tries in a short time.
talk.refused: Said by the text program when the server refused for a reason it has no sentence for; {error} is the short code of the refusal, shown as it is.
talk.proof.prompt: The prompt of the hidden line where the person types their password to prove it is them, in the text program; it ends with a space because the person types right after it.
talk.proof.nothing_waits: Said by the text program when a proof is given but no request waits for one.
talk.proof.busy: Said by the text program when the server is checking too many passwords at once and the person must try again.
talk.unknown_command: Said by the text program when the person types a command starting with a slash that it does not have; /quit is the command that leaves the program and must stay as written.
talk.unreachable: Said by the text program when the server cannot be reached; {url} is the address tried, shown as it is.
talk.not_trusted: Said by the text program, after it cannot be reached, when the reason is that the assistant's security certificate is not trusted by this computer.
talk.unpaired_now: Said by the text program when the assistant no longer knows this computer (its access was taken back); the person presses the Enter key to leave the program.
